areas.fix_scope: One commit per problem, the failing test first. Order: R-lock first (a merge of an unrebuilt head is the worst outcome), then R-chain, R-owed, R-conflict, R-copystuck, the notification. Line numbers in the evidence are from fa1a86f: leftovers7-merge (merged at a2caf52, its report in /tmp/frbench/wave7g6a-fix-merge.json) changed pr-executor.ts, dependent-branches.ts, merge.ts and docs.ts since, so re-find each place at HEAD and reuse what it added (taskBranchName, cleanAfterCutShortRun, the retry pass's check-first path and its Update, the rebuild card's Merge/Redo in request-words.ts) rather than duplicating it. R-lock: one exported worktree lock (from pr-executor or a small module beside it) used by PrExecutor's rebuilds and by ReviewedPrMerge's git steps in a task worktree; a rebuild that voids a record must also make a merge call already under way for that record end without merging the unrebuilt head (check the head sha the host would merge, or hold the lock across the call). R-owed: persist owed rebuilds (a new migration 0008, or a column on merge_record) with the SQLite and Postgres suite (packages/state/test/suite.ts) and a restart test; data-model.md says what the new state means. R-conflict: the watcher reads mergeable for open task pull requests (bounded: only when the base moved, not every poll for every PR), files one card per pull request (deduped across polls and restarts), and the Overview row stops offering a Merge that cannot work; the compose.ts wiring is one small hunk. R-copystuck: a new CopyView field with the reason, GET /projects/:id/files carries it (fake daemon in the same commit, a real-daemon.test.ts case), and the Files line says the copy stopped following and why. Words: polish (wave 13, after this wave) owns the wording; where a new sentence is unavoidable follow design §5 (one sentence read at a glance, CHF only, no ids) and list it in notes_for_other_areas. apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts and apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts are append-only (own describe block). Do not change runner.ts, executor.ts, recovery.ts, critic.ts, session-review.ts, intake.ts, start-check.ts, plan-tasks.ts or conversation/agent.ts (leftovers7-session's, merged), nor web-access.ts, agent/sdk.ts, enforcement/hooks.ts, billing-pick.ts, credential-choice.ts, start-blocked.ts, triggers.ts, browser/profile.ts (leftovers7-web's, running beside you). compose.ts: leftovers7-web owns the credential wake and the chooser; you may add one small hunk for the conflict watcher's wiring and one for the notifier of a later merge, and say so. Docs: runtime.md (rebuilds, the merge lock, the conflict notice, the copy), data-model.md, ADR 0111 (its known gaps at 'Known gaps' close) and ADR 0113 ('Known limits': the copy that stops following) amendments.

problems: [major] TM-1: a redo from main (the conflict notice's or the rebuild card's Redo) or 'Drop the branch and retry from scratch' whose run changes nothing, on a task with an open pull request, force-pushes main's head to the task branch: the task is done with an empty pull request that the app offers for Merge (bench run 2 of the merge2 fix-up: PR #4 merged with no diff). Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge2.json new_problems[0]; pr-executor.ts execute: `!commit.committed && !existingPr` (:878 at ce13bb1) is the only no-change check, and with `dropped` the branch starts at the base.

[minor] TM-2: cleanAfterCutShortRun runs before conflictAnswer: a person who resolves a rebase conflict in the task folder (the card's 'branch only on this computer' steps) and answers 'I resolved it' with the rebase still in progress has the half-done resolution aborted. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-merge.json non_blocking[1], /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge.json not_done[1] (suggested fix: skip abortUnfinished while the task's last conflict answer is 'resolved' and not consumed).

[minor] TM-3: an unconsumed 'dropped' answer (the conflict card's Drop, a Redo from main) drops a paused run's work in progress at the next run: if the redo's run pauses (budget, a question) before review, the next run starts from main again (executeIn: wip = dropped ? null : …). Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge.json not_done[5] and new_problems[1]; the fix-up's reason not to consume the mark at branch creation (the next run would merge the old conflicting branch into the work in progress) is the constraint to respect.

[minor] TM-4: Merge pressed while a rebuild is owed because the task's folder holds changes nobody committed: the record waits 'queued' and the row reads 'Merging…' with no reason until the folder is cleaned; meanwhile 'dependent branch not rebuilt: its worktree has uncommitted changes' is logged as a WARN at every poll. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fix-leftovers7-merge2.json not_done[0]; /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-merge2.json non_blocking[2] (bench walk 3 step 14) and [7].

[minor] TM-5: possible watcher stall (not reproduced): lookFor().baseChange, keepsOwnChange and mergeChecked's update path wait on inWorktree, and PrTaskExecutor.execute holds the folder for a whole run; a done task redone while its record is queued or waiting_checks would make retryWaitingMerges, which the watcher's poll awaits, block every poll until the redo ends (no PR events, copy refreshes or conflict notices meanwhile). Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-merge2.json non_blocking[3]; /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge2.json not_done[1].

[minor] TM-6: copyStoppedOf (loop/docs.ts) matches git's English messages, and GitOps (capabilities githost/git.ts) runs git with the process's locale: on a git that prints in another language the Files line falls back to 'Git could not bring it to what is merged…' without the file names. Check the other places that parse git's messages (rebase and merge conflict files) for the same dependence. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-merge2.json non_blocking[4]; /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge2.json not_done[0].

[minor] TM-7: a record whose left-to-you sentence said something else (rebuilt_without's 'reviewed with #A's changes…' warning, 'builds on #X, which was not merged: merge #X first') loses it after a conflict is resolved: conflict_resolved sets the sentence to ''. The row then offers a plain Merge without the earlier warning. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-merge2.json non_blocking[5]; /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge2.json not_done[2].

[minor] TM-8: the project page's Create a repository dialog files its pending card on Preview; closing the dialog with × or Escape leaves that card open in the Inbox (CreateRepoDialog.tsx finish() does not answer result.pendingId). Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge.json new_problems[0] (walk-repo-B.json 'afterPreview', steps/05-b-preview-shown.png).

[minor] TM-9: CopyRecord.stopped (the copy's 'stopped following' state, a file in the copy's .git) is persisted state with no restart test (validation rule 4); the bench showed it survives restart-daemon.mjs. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-merge2.json non_blocking[1].

Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-web.json non_blocking[2].

[minor] TR-3: compose.ts credentialWaitNow builds the pick without the task's answered state and with modelTier fixed to 'sonnet': a task whose person questions were answered still gets the askPerson need, so the Start check can say 'Nothing can run yet' while the real run would go to the subscription. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-web.json non_blocking[4].

[minor] TR-5: intake.ts onlyWebsitesLines with an empty 'only' list gives the planner '…only these websites and their subdomains: . Plan no research…' (model-facing; a sibling of R-failopen). Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-web.json non_blocking[5]; intake.ts:473.

[minor] TR-6: person-questions.ts isPersonTask still matches PERSONS_ANSWER on legacy titles without the RECORDED_ANSWER exception (a sibling of R-personsanswers); and RECORDED_ANSWER removes the need for a whole text, so 'Follow the owner's decision in docs/x and get the owner's confirmation before deploying' loses the confirmation need unless NEEDS_PERSON catches it. decisions: W15-01 (only the safety part, until the owner answers W15-112): an ownership marker in the status and scaffold PR bodies; a project never pushes to, comments on or lists another project's status or scaffold PR; while another project's status PR is open on fr/status this project writes none and its status stays in the app (one log line says why); with none open, today's behaviour; a legacy PR without a marker belongs to a project only when it is the only one on this install linked to the repository. No per-project branch and no second PR.

W15-02: a local commit ahead of origin on a done task's branch that is not Forerunner's own (its work-in-progress commit, its base merge, a rebuild whose push failed) holds the rebuild with one sentence and is never reset; Forerunner's own unpushed states rebuild as today.

W15-03: a dependency whose rebuild was busy, held, failed or conflicted holds the tasks that build on it as owed in the same pass; a clean same-own-change rebuild clears a stale rebuild_conflict (sentence, last_outcome and card).

W15-04: the Tasks tab's Redo on a done task with an open merge card answers that card as the card's own Redo does (redo from main, the card closed 'redone') in the same transaction, and starts no session: the owner question on Tasks-row actions stays open.

W15-05: the person's approval stays recorded and the merge goes on once the folder is clean; the held-by-changes fact is persisted on the record at the poll and shown on the row before and after the press.

W15-06: both 'I resolved it' and 'Drop the branch and retry from scratch' start or queue a session through resumeWork, as every Inbox answer that makes a task runnable does (design §3.8); Cancel starts nothing.
W15-07: a null mergeable is re-read within the same poll (a few seconds apart, capped at about 15 s in all), never by a busy loop.
W15-08: ids that code reads move to a hidden HTML-comment marker (one form shared with W15-01's ownership marker); the reader accepts the old visible form for PRs opened by earlier versions.

W15-55: one label per merge record outcome in task-words.ts's merge-state branch (now w15-merge's), agreeing with the Overview row (design §2: one status map), including the states W15-03 and W15-05 add.

W15-64: emptiedSentence's two failing forms, 'main already has this change.' and the up_to_date PR comment are reworded to the texts in the acceptance; owedFolderSentence was checked against design §5 and stays (W15-05's tests can assert it).
W15-68: the waiting_checks sentence and label are chosen by the outcome's status ('#4 merges once GitHub answers.' for an unreachable host).
root_causes: packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts: the status branch and PR belong to the repository, not to a project (fixed name, PR reused by head only, ownership approved for any fr/status PR, no marker).

packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts rebuildDependents/rebuildIn: a busy middle does not hold its dependents; a local commit is reset to origin; only uncommitted changes count as the person's.

packages/runtime/src/session/dependent-branches.ts and loop/merge.ts: conflict state is cleared only from last_outcome 'conflict'; a new review or a clean rebuild leaves stale cards; the watcher reads mergeable once per 60 s poll and drops null.

packages/runtime/src/daemon/pull-requests.ts / loop/merge-mode.ts: the merge route answers from canMerge before the folder state is known, and the record never carries that state until the merge step runs.
packages/runtime/src/session/pr-answers.ts: only the rebuild card's Redo resumes work; the rebase-conflict card has no words of its own.
packages/capabilities/src/githost/git.ts: parsed git messages assume English where untranslated is not set; folders made before 29e0c81 keep the machine's autocrlf.

packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-words.ts's merge-state branch and the merge-side sentences (merge.ts, pr-executor.ts emptiedSentence, pull-requests.ts rows): labels and sentences read a subset of the merge record (any last_outcome but 'conflict' reads 'waiting for you to merge'; the waiting_checks sentence whatever the status) and offer ways out no button gives.

decisions: W15-12: a tool output whose shape cannot be confirmed and that holds a resolved secret is denied with a reason and an audit row; never pass a resolved secret. The SDK ships the shapes as TypeScript types only (sdk-tools.d.ts), so conformance is checked with one typed fixture per allowed built-in tool, which pnpm typecheck re-checks on every SDK upgrade.

W15-13: one rule for the write cap and the cut-off retry: a call is paid only from the money below the run's wrap-up line (as web search already is); the raised cap applies to the retried call only; complete tool_use blocks of a cut reply may be kept (U-085 amendment) if it stays safe (a cut block is never run).

W15-15/W15-17: the web search offer is decided once at the run's start (affordable or not, with the loop's own arithmetic) and its definition stays byte-identical while it is offered; the limits stay in code: max_uses fixed at the start, its full worst case counted on every call that offers it, and the tool dropped once (one cache rewrite) at the first call where the searches left or the money below the line no longer cover it; never 'told in text' instead (ADR 0107's 'a search never eats the reserve' holds).

W15-14/W15-16: 'Left to do' counts only what the criteria still need; the wrap-up's log line and its model-facing text say what is really true (ADR 0112 amendment), and their amounts under a centime read 'less than CHF 0.01'.
W15-18: estimates get a deterministic size factor from the outcome and criteria; the plan card and the Start dialog keep showing the same figure (R-estimates).
W15-20: actual_cost_usd_micro stays the work-only budget counter; a separate ledger-based 'spent' figure is what the person reads.
W15-21: per-call booking on the task and the Run row is atomic; a person's action during a run must not fail on the version bump.

W15-59, W15-69, W15-70: w15-run adds the session outcome's fields (the tasks the person cancelled, a paused count, waitingPrs split into checks pending and GitHub not answering) to runner.ts and session.ended, and writes their sentences in session/result.ts and event-lines.ts endedCounts.
root_causes: packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts: per-call sizing (write room, cut-off floor, max_uses) is recomputed each call from rules that contradict each other and ignore the wrap-up line or the prompt cache.

packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts and executor.ts: the handoff parser and the pause rule treat any listed line as unfinished work; the wrap-up words describe a spend threshold while the code triggers on spend plus the next call's worst case; amounts are formatted without moneyWords.
packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts searchPlanFor: the brief's search line is decided without the money the loop checks.
packages/runtime/src/estimates/model.ts: estimates know only specialist and tier; a killed run is taken as a sample.

packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts and executor.ts: spend reaches the task and the Run row only when the run returns, and reviews never reach the task's figure; the session outcome has no cancelled tasks, no paused count and one waitingPrs count, so session/result.ts and event-lines.ts endedCounts cannot say what happened.

W15-14 (budget-pause.test.ts and real-daemon with the stand-in researcher at Budget 0.15): a run that hears the wrap-up and lists only 'Nothing for the acceptance criteria.' and an 'Optionally …' extra is reviewed and Done; no 'paused at its budget' card; parseHandoff on the live report returns no blocking items; the wrap-up request text asks for criteria-only items or 'nothing'.

W15-15 (loop-web-search.test.ts with PromptCacheSim taught the API's web-search/max_uses rules; a stand-in model that searches on every call): every request of one run that offers web_search sends a byte-identical web_search definition (max_uses and lists fixed at the run's start); the tool is dropped at most once in the run and never re-added; each call's cache_read >= the previous call's cache_read + cache_creation except at that one drop; the run's searches never exceed the task's searches left (ten over all its runs); every call that offers the tool counts the full max_uses in its pre-call worst case; no search is paid from the reserve kept to finish (spend when the wrap-up is told <= the run's line; the tool is gone from that call on); no limit relies on text alone.

W15-27: TR-15 as ADR 0112's amendment of 2026-11-09 designs it; a changed head or attempt falls back to today's rerun.
W15-28: the runtime decides between a questions card and a sign-off before the critic files anything.

W15-33: the plan card's 'reads no website' line is one function in plan-tasks.ts beside cannotRunHere, in a field the card already renders.

root_causes: packages/runtime/src/loop/try-plan.ts: a prose command ends at a stop word with no arguments and is run bare; expectsError reads only its own sentence.

packages/runtime/src/loop/critic.ts: the review's evidence is built from the task's title and outcome and the last run's result only (no site rule, no earlier runs' pages); the sign-off is filed before the runtime decides the card.
packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts / budget-card.ts: a refused review keeps no result, so the next session reruns the specialist.
packages/runtime/src/brief.ts, session/executor.ts, capabilities/src/web/fetch.ts: no date and no read time anywhere a specialist or the critic looks.
evals/registry/specialists/*/specialist.md: an unconditional default output file; packages/runtime/src/session/intake.ts: the empty-list rule says what not to plan, never what to plan instead.

The words of reviews and tries: the sent-back line built from the summary's first 100 characters, ruledSummary's dead branches, a raw verdict in the Critic column, Playwright's exception text, a package.json that is not there, markdown tables and one row per read in the drawer.

One commit per item: the failing test first at the person's boundary named in its acceptance line (a real-daemon case, a composed daemon test, a UI test, or the unit test of the function that writes the sentence), then the fix, then the siblings (validation rule 8; log what you find in new_problems). problems: [fix] W15B-01 (major, data loss): a resume or a redo from main of a branch whose pull request is open (the Tasks-row Redo of a done task, with or without a merge card; a Try again) resets the task's folder and drops a commit the person made there without a word; Evidence: wave15a-review-w15-merge:non_blocking[6], wave15a-fixup-w15-merge:not_done[1] and new_problems[1], wave15a-merge:problems_left[1] (4); Root cause at 3600089: packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts executeIn resets at two sites without asking folderHold (:277-310; callers only :2000 and merge.ts:1930): (1) the resume with no work in progress, :1011 createBranch(branch, origin/branch); (2) the redo from main (a Redo with an open merge card closes it with REDO_FROM_BASE, commands/task.ts:308-322; conflictAnswer reads 'dropped', :2834): the branch keeps its name while its PR is open (:968) and :1087 createBranch(branch, depsBase ?? origin/base) runs checkout -B (git.ts:496) over it. :922 cleanAfterCutShortRun sets uncommitted changes aside under failedRef (kept, silently).

decisions: W15B-01: hold, never reset and never bring the person's commit along unasked (as W15-02's rebuild; ADR 0111). Before the reset at :1011, and before the one at :1087 when the branch keeps its name because its PR is open, folderHold 'commits' ends the run before any model call: nothing reset, no spend; executeIn returns { outcome: 'needs_human', summary: <sentence>, costUsdMicro: 0, branch } as its dependency-base refusal does (:1039, :1079). The runner (unchanged) sets the task needs_human with that reason and files the cannot-run card ('"X" could not run. <sentence>', Try again / Cancel task); the row reads 'Needs your decision: it could not run' and offers Answer, Edit, Cancel. So the sentence names Try again, never Redo: resume 'Its task folder has a commit that is not on GitHub: push it or undo it, then press Try again.'; redo from main 'Its task folder has a commit that is not on GitHub, and doing the task again from main would drop it: undo it or keep it on another branch, then press Try again.'. The session goes on with other tasks. The sentence reaches the row, the card and the session log only as the run's summary: no edit to task-words.ts, task-display.ts, event-lines.ts or runner.ts (w15-words' W15B-79 makes the log's task.finished line say the run's sentence). Not built in run B: an immediate answer at the Redo itself (commands/task.ts task.reopen with a folder port; a hint for run C, where D6 changes what Redo does). Uncommitted changes stay as built (set aside under failedRef, kept) unless the executor can tell cheaply that the last run finished; the report says which. Tasks-row actions still start no work (D6 is run C's). The owner is asked to confirm hold (new owner question).

W15B-02: the safety part only (W5-40 stays open). One guard where every start passes: compose.ts startSession (:3300) refuses an archived project with one sentence ('The project "<name>" was removed, so nothing of it runs.' or the fixer's §5 words), which covers POST /sessions, the chat's session.start, a credential wake, a budget resume, a plan approval's start and a handover job; POST /sessions refuses at once with the same sentence before requestStart (no session row); credentialWaits.wake skips a removed project and drops its wait (the next tick does not retry it); refreshJobSchedules schedules no handover for it; the intake's propose refuses it and its filing re-reads the status right before the insert, so a plan drafted during the Undo is never filed; the creation's Undo is refused while a session of that project runs ('Cannot be undone now: a session of <name> is running. Stop it first.'); ProjectPage reads the status GET /projects/:id already returns and says 'This project was removed.' with no Start session or Create a repository. No api-types or views.ts change. D6 (run C) removes the wake's own start; until then this guard stops it.

W15B-03: coverage, not a fix. One composed conversation test at the chat's boundary with a scripted chat model that obeys a questions card's quoted words: a card that orders a wider site rule, a task cancel and a budget raise ends the turn in the read-back with nothing changed, and the request's system text carries the data rule. Expected to pass at 3600089: committed as a guard, and the report says it passed at once (rule 8 is for fixes). If a code-enforced part fails, that is a real bug: the case stays failing first, the fix goes in the gate (packages/commands/src/executor.ts decideSteps, or a spec's narrows or limit flag in commands/settings.ts), siblings after. conversation/agent.ts is not edited in run B (run C's D3). A narrowing the card's words ask for acts at once by design; no code can tell it from the person's own: that is W15B-80, later for run C.
W15B-05: about 15 s of re-reads per poll in all, through the watcher's clock; stop() ends the wait; no GitHub call after stop.

W15B-07: PlanTaskView.note (append-only) with 'Reads no website: this project's "only these websites" list is empty. Add websites in Settings, or Change the plan.'; plan-tasks.ts reads the rule from deps.estimate.project.settings and a new PlanTasksDeps.readsWeb(name), passed at server.ts:1861-1871 from the registry; the fake daemon in the same commit; InboxPage renders it beside runsOn.
W15B-08: tests only; a failing case is a real bug, fixed in the same commit.

Not in this area (the owner's answers of 2026-11-09 give them to run C): W15B-04 (the Docs note while another project's status PR is open; D1), W15B-06 (the chat reads the status kept in the app; D3), W15B-09 (a project named only as a word in the chat's card selection; D3) and W15B-80 (a narrowing a card's words ask for; D3).

status 'archived' is read only by Changes: nothing that starts work (a press, a wake, a schedule), files a plan or shows a project page knows a project was removed, and the creation's Undo does not ask whether its session runs.
The chat's card facts (W15-30) carry model text into a model that holds command tools, with a rule but no hostile test of the gate behind it.
The watcher's re-read was written per PR with a bare setTimeout, outside the clock stop() controls.
The plan card reads only per-install limitations; a per-project rule has no field, and its deps do not say who reads the web.
Run A left tests at internal seams where the binding rules ask for the person's boundary, the Inbox's options and a restart.

areas.title: Chat treats every record as data and keeps the first word fast: what today's read tools return is quoted as data and scanned; a change the model asks for in a turn that read a record, or whose facts quote a card's words in full, is read back first (stops of the running session excepted, Stop all read back); the record channel joins the injection suite; the waiting merges come from the app's own records, so no turn waits on GitHub; the facts carry the person's own date and time; one scope function says whose records chat may read
problems: [major (security)] D3-3: What the read tools return (a specialist's report, which can quote a web page, the critic's words, card questions, the last session's text) reaches the chat model unmarked: not wrapped as data and not scanned, in a model that holds command tools; recall would widen that to every record. Owner's words: "recall anything that has been recorded" (the round's rule: text from any record is data, never instructions); Where: read-tools.ts:38 ok() sets no untrusted, :159-166 (reports, review, cards verbatim); packages/runtime/src/enforcement/hooks.ts:478-490 wraps only results marked untrusted.

[major (security)] D3-4: Nothing in code tells a change the person asked for from one a record asked for: in a turn whose model read a run report, or whose facts quote a card's words in full, a low-risk change the model calls (a new task, a note for the next session's brief, a session start under the costly line, a narrowing setting) acts at once. W15B-80 (run B: 'a design choice for that rework', left to run C's D3). Owner's words: "recall anything that has been recorded"; Where: packages/commands/src/executor.ts:284-298 decideSteps (askFromChat only for task changes), packages/commands/src/confirmation.ts:30-39, packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts narrowingActsAtOnce, packages/commands/src/commands/session.ts:116-121, packages/runtime/src/loop/ports.ts:280-297 (CommandTurn knows nothing of what the turn read). A 'stop everything' the model calls after reading a record would also stop all work with no read-back (denial of work), although the header's Stop all asks once (design section 3.1).

[major] D3-5: On a repository project every chat turn waits for GitHub's list of open pull requests before the model is called: with GitHub slow or unreachable the first word waits for the client's timeout, whatever was asked. Owner's words: "We are trying to both balance and be flexible with time and tokens spent vs quality and relevance of the reponse."; Where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:4084-4097 openPullRequests, awaited at packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1399-1407.

[minor] D3-6: 'Yesterday', 'last week' and 'on Monday' are worked out in UTC: the facts carry now as a UTC timestamp and the person's time zone is stored but unused. Owner's words: "quality and relevance of the reponse"; Where: agent.ts:1348-1350 (now: clock.nowIso()), packages/state/src/schema.ts:132 (human.timezone).

[minor] D3-8: The files block tells the model 'the person merges it on GitHub', while Merge is in the app. Owner's words: "quality and relevance of the reponse"; Where: project-facts.ts:446 filesBlock.

[minor (privacy)] D3-17: Today's read tools find a project by name among every project on the store, with no owner filter, and the per-turn lessons reach the model unwrapped (only doc excerpts are wrapped, agent.ts:1524). Owner's words: "recall anything that has been recorded" (the round's rule: only this person's records, and every record is data); Where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/read-tools.ts:41-52 (projectOf); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1485-1488 (lessons), :1524 (the one wrapUntrusted).
decisions: The waiting merges come from the app's own merge records, not from GitHub: '# Your files' names the folder, then the done tasks whose merge waits for the person ('Waiting for your Merge: "Style the page": <the record's sentence>') and those merged, from merge_record (Merge and the watcher keep it); a done task with a pull request and no record is listed as today without a state; files_list asks the host for the open pull requests only when it is called (L-17 on demand; 'Whether its pull requests are merged is not known: GitHub did not answer.' when the host does not answer); 'the person merges it on GitHub' goes. Why: the first word never waits on GitHub; the records are true within the watcher's minute; the host's answer is one call away.

Quoted as data: every result of today's tasks_list, task_get, session_last and files_list is marked untrusted (records: source agent_output, origin 'record:<kind>'), and the per-turn lessons are wrapped like the doc excerpts (agent.ts:1524), so the hooks wrap them in the data envelope and scan them. A command outcome may carry the same mark (CommandOutcome.untrusted, append-only) when its answer quotes text the person did not write (d1109-onerepo-link's 'used elsewhere' answer quotes a repository's marker); loop/commands.ts passes it to the tool result. d1109-chat-recall marks recall's results the same way. Why: records are written by agents and pages; the round's security rule.

The read-back after records, in code: CommandTurn gains recordsRead (append-only; read when the command tools build each call's context, packages/runtime/src/loop/commands.ts:283), and CommandContext gains it too. It is set when any tool result of the turn carries the untrusted mark (a read tool, later recall, a command answer that quotes such text), when the turn's facts list a card in full whose words Forerunner did not write (a specialist's question, the critic's words), and when a doc excerpt or a lesson in the facts is flagged by the scanner. In such a turn executor.decideSteps answers needs_yes for every change the model calls, whatever its risk: one read-back with Yes and No. Stops: session.stop for the running session ('stop') and 'stop after this task' still act at once (design section 3.9, the safe direction); session.stop with scope all (Stop all) is read back once with the header's own question ('Stop every running session now? No session starts until you allow it again.', design section 3.1), since a record must not stop all work by itself; the person's own typed 'stop everything' is the parser's and acts at once as today. A turn with none of these is unchanged, and so are the parser's own commands. d1109-chat-depth's gate reads the same flag, so a record never starts a thorough answer by itself. Why: W15B-80 (left by run B to run C's D3); design section 3.9 already reads changes back; one Yes is the price of never acting on a record's words.

The person's own time: '# Now' gains 'today: Monday 9 November 2026, 23:30 (Europe/Zurich)' beside today's UTC now, from human.timezone (todayLine in project-facts.ts). Why: 'yesterday' and 'last week' are the person's days, not UTC's; d1109-chat-recall's windowOf uses the same zone; the line is volatile and uncached, so the cached prefix does not move.

Scope: one function scopeOf(humanId) in packages/runtime/src/conversation/scope.ts gives the projects whose records this person may read (their own and those shared with them); read-tools.ts's projectOf calls it, and d1109-chat-recall's recall does too; wave 8's collab-privacy replaces its rule in that one place. Why: AGENTS.md privacy; today's read tools list every project on the store.

The record channel of pnpm test:injection: INJECTION_CHANNELS gains 'record' (a case's text is planted in the store and reaches the model through today's read tools and the facts: a run report through task_get, a card question listed in full, a session result through session_last, a doc section in the excerpts); d1109-chat-recall adds the cases that reach the model through recall. Why: the injection suite tests what reaches a model; records were not a channel.

Keep today's behaviour: the parser path, W15-30's card scope and its rules, the 12-turn history, the docs and lessons budgets, docs/status.md left out, no web tools in chat, Make this a task, the fast pass's model, effort and thinking, the turn budget (ADR 0091).

problems: [major (owner decision)] D4-1: A task whose estimate alone is more than the session's work budget never runs: the plan leaves it out, a session where it is the only ready task ends at once with 'Nothing could run: "Long report" needs about CHF 1.20, more than this session's work budget of CHF 0.32. Start a session with a larger budget.', the Start dialog and POST /sessions refuse that start, and beside other work it is 'Left for next time' in every session of that size. Owner's words: "it should get a warning, but it should get done anyway." Where: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:3741-3762 (cutPlanToBudget), :1203 (the start's cut), :1434-1439 (each re-plan's), :1477-1490 (the queue runs only what the cut kept); packages/runtime/src/session/start-check.ts:105-113, :152-155; packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:1532-1543; packages/runtime/src/session/result.ts:286-302, :321-333.

[major (money)] D4-6: A task that resumes from its kept work is planned at its whole estimate again unless it has a budget of its own: after it spent CHF 4.00 of work, a CHF 6.00 task still reads 'needs about CHF 6.00' in the Start dialog and the plan and stays larger than a session that could finish it. A task that starts over (Redo, Try again, a conflict Redo from main, a review that sent it back) starts from nothing, so for it the whole estimate is the honest figure, and spend alone cannot tell the two apart (actual_cost_usd_micro only grows, packages/state/src/repos/task.ts:104-114). Owner's words: "such that the work can be continued in the next run"; Where: packages/runtime/src/estimates/model.ts:883-910 (planEstimateUsdMicro, withinTaskBudget: only a task's own budget lowers the figure).

[major (owner decision, words)] D4-7: The Start dialog refuses Start when the only ready task is larger than the session's work budget ('Nothing can run within this budget: "X" needs about CHF 6.00.') and beside other work tells the person to give the session a larger budget or the task a smaller one; it never says that the task starts, works until the budget is used and pauses with its work kept. Owner's words: "it should get a warning, but it should get done anyway." Where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/start-blocked.ts:161-167; apps/ui/src/pages/project/StartSessionDialog.tsx:181-211 (the over-budget lines), :133-139 (planSentence names only the runnable tasks), :313 and :502 (Start off); packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:1404-1452 (the view has no field for the larger task).

[minor] D4-8: The plan card shows 'about CHF 6.00' beside such a task and nothing more: the person approves a plan whose first session will pause without being told. Owner's words: "it should get a warning" (the Start dialog keeps a clear warning; the plan card too). Where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/plan-tasks.ts:97-147 (planTaskViews); apps/ui/src/pages/InboxPage.tsx:302-400 (IntakeCard, the runs-on line :385-393).

[minor] D4-9: Chat's 'start a session' refuses with the Start dialog's blocker sentence for such a task, and its read-back never warns. Owner's words: "it should get a warning, but it should get done anyway." Where: packages/commands/src/commands/session.ts:99-102 (refuseBlockedStart), :106-109 (startAsk).

[words] D4-10: The result's 'Nothing could run: "X" needs about CHF 1.20, more than this session's work budget of CHF 0.32. Start a session with a larger budget.' becomes untrue once such a task runs, and the session log has no line for taking the larger task with what is left. Owner's words: "it should get a warning, but it should get done anyway." Where: packages/runtime/src/session/result.ts:286-302, :321-333; packages/runtime/src/daemon/event-lines.ts; packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts lineOf (:559-640).
decisions: The pick (OS-2): a ready task is larger than one session when its plan figure alone is more than the session's work budget (the cap less the review reserve). cutPlanToBudget keeps today's greedy cut for every task that fits and returns, apart, the first larger task in the planner's order (`oversized`, with its full figure); any other larger task is left out with the reason 'one_large', a fitting task left out keeps 'after_others'. The runner holds the larger task out of the queue and takes it when the queue is empty and a re-plan adds nothing (so tasks that become ready meanwhile also run first), with what is left of the work budget, when that is at least a fifth of the work budget (OVERSIZED_MIN_ROOM_SHARE = 0.2, beside WRAP_UP_SHARE) and no-new-work is not set; else it is left out with 'no_room'. When taken it joins the plan row (a versioned change, reason 'took "X", larger than this session's work budget, with what is left') with its planned figure set to that room, so the session review measures what it was allowed to spend; at autonomy 0 and 1 it is in the approved set (onlyThese). The start check calls the same function and reports the larger task with the room the tasks before it leave (the ready ones and the 'later' ones) and each left-out task's reason. Why: the owner's 'it should get done anyway'; every task that fits keeps today's behaviour and is done and reviewed whole this session; a larger task can never fit, so starting it is the only way it gets done; one a session because two cannot both get a useful share; a fifth is the share a run keeps to wrap up, so less room would be mostly reserve.

Start is never refused for it (OS-2): start-blocked's firstBlocker no longer treats a larger task as a blocker (the :161-167 branch goes), so the Start dialog keeps Start on and POST /sessions, Approve and start and chat's session.start start the session; the start check keeps the task in overBudget with its reason and adds oversized. The refusal's removal, the warning's sentence and the dialog's use of it are one area's work, so no merged head starts the task without a warning or warns of a start it refuses. Why: the owner's "it should get a warning, but it should get done anyway"; the adversarial check found the D4 design's OV-1 'POST /sessions is not refused' could not pass in an area that did not own start-blocked.ts.

What is left of the estimate, for kept work only (OS-1): estimateLeftUsdMicro(task, kept) beside planEstimateUsdMicro gives a task that resumes from its kept work its estimate less the cost of that kept work: the cost of the consecutive runs, ending with its latest, that each paused at a budget with their work kept (refs/forerunner/wip/<task> or the folder's work-in-progress commit), the same condition under which its next brief carries '## Where the last run stopped' (task-context.ts:250-258). Once that cost reached the estimate it is a fifth of the estimate, marked estimatePassed (the estimate was too low and what is left is not known); a task's own budget still caps it (withinTaskBudget unchanged). Every other task keeps today's figure, whatever it spent before: one redone from main (Redo, Try again, a conflict Redo), one a review sent back, one that failed and was tried again before it paused (only the runs after its last start over count). One function for the planner, the start check, the plan card and the chat. The learner still takes no sample from a paused task (ADR 0112, the cost amendment point 4). Why: work that goes on from a commit needs what is left; work that starts over needs its whole estimate again, and planning it at estimate less earlier spend would let the Start dialog, the plan card and D6's join-if-fits admit it as fitting when it does not.

The sentences (OS-3, design §5 rule 10): packages/runtime/src/daemon/oversize-words.ts writes every sentence about a task larger than a session from the start check's facts. oversizedSentence: '"Build the shop" needs about CHF 6.00, more than this session's work budget of CHF 4.00: it works until that budget is used, keeps its work, and asks you to continue.'; after other tasks '"Build the shop" needs about CHF 6.00, more than this session's work budget of CHF 4.00: after the other tasks it works with about CHF 2.80, keeps its work, and asks you to continue.'; a task that already spent work names 'about CHF 2.00 more (CHF 4.00 spent so far)'; no room '"Build the shop" needs about CHF 6.00, more than this session's work budget: the tasks before it leave too little to start it, so it waits for the next session.'; a second larger task '"Big two" needs about CHF 9.00, more than this session's work budget: one task that large runs a session, so it waits for the next one.'. oversizedPlanNote: 'More than a session's work budget (CHF 4.00): it pauses with its work kept and asks you to continue.' (at most 100 characters). oversizedAsk for the chat. CHF only, 'about' for estimates, no ids. The start-check route returns oversized { taskId, title, estimate, room, spent?, sentence } or null and each overBudget entry's why and sentence; oversizedPlanClause gives the dialog's plan sentence its clause about the larger task. Why: the owner's warning, said the same way everywhere and true now (it follows the runner's own hold, OS-2).

The Start dialog (OS-4): Start stays on; the plan sentence names the larger task ('This session runs "A" (about CHF 0.12), then works on "Build the shop" with what is left.'; alone 'This session works on "Build the shop" until its work budget is used.'); the amber note shows the daemon's sentence (testid start-session-oversized) and the reasons of any other task left out; the dialog's own over-budget sentences of today (after run B's list form, W15-38) are replaced by the daemon's. Why: the dialog keeps a clear warning without refusing what the owner wants done. d1109-starts-engine later rebuilds planSentence from its own cut list and keeps this clause by calling oversizedPlanClause.

The plan card (OS-5): planTaskViews gives a task whose figure alone is more than the project's session work budget (its session cap less the reserve) an oversized note, shown under the task as the runs-on line is (after w15-tail's note). Why: 'the plan card too': the person approves knowing the first session will pause.

The chat (OS-6): session.start's read-back adds the warning through a startWarning port beside startBlocked ('Start a session on Shop (up to CHF 5.00)? "Build the shop" needs more than its work budget of CHF 4.00: it pauses with its work kept and asks you to continue.') and no longer refuses such a start. Why: the chat is the Start dialog's sibling (validation rule 8). The start itself stays session.start's; d1109-starts-engine makes it a person start (D6).

The result and the log (OS-7): the W6-23 branch 'Nothing could run: ... Start a session with a larger budget.' goes (a larger task alone now runs); a second larger task left out ('one_large') or one the tasks before it left no room for ('no_room') is named in 'Left for next time' with its reason's sentence from oversize-words.ts; the session log says 'Took "Build the shop", larger than this session's work budget, with about CHF 2.80 left.' once, when it is taken. The pause's own sentences, the run again in the session and the card are d1109-oversize-pause's. Why: the result and the log say what happened (design section 5 rule 4).

Who starts (D6, owner-confirmed in the third follow-up of 2026-11-09): nothing in this area starts a session. The larger task runs in a session the person started (Start, Approve and start, chat's 'start a session', Continue on a card) or, until d1109-starts-engine merges, in one that starts as today. No sentence here says that a task goes on by itself. Why: D6, 'the person says when a session starts'.

decisions: Place: Sessions is the first entry behind More ▾ (Sessions, Plan, Docs, Reviews, Costs, Data), at /projects/:id/sessions; the Overview's Last result links 'All N sessions' from two sessions on, and every session page links 'All sessions'. Why: design §6 keeps four primary tabs for the daily loop; the list is looked back on; one click from the two places a person thinks of sessions; no clutter on Home or the Overview.

The heading is the count only: '14 sessions'. There is no 'in all' total: the Costs tab is the one place for a project's totals (they also hold chat and planning outside sessions and, after a join, the closed project's line), and a second total that differs from Costs by the chat spend would be one fact in two places (design section 5 rule 10). Why: the owner asked what each session did, spent and how it ended; each row carries its own CHF.

A row is two lines and one link: the gist sentence first (≤ 100 characters, design §5), then 'when · how long · task counts · how it ended · CHF on which credential' (and 'started by itself …' when not a plain Start). Why: exactly what the owner listed (what each did, spent, how it ended), read at a glance; the full result stays on the session page (§5.10).

The working session(s) sit above the list with live progress, using the project's working sentence ('Working on "Style the page" (3 of 7 done)') and 'CHF … so far'; no Stop on the row. Why: one status map (§2); Stop lives on the session page and the header (§3.1, §3.7). workingWords is one function in session-list.ts: until d1109-run-visible (sub-run C5) re-points it at its runText it uses the project status's working sentence (project-status.ts workingOn), never a wording of its own, so the list never says what runs now in a third way.

Order: newest first by start (created_at, then id); 20 a page, at most 50; 'Show older sessions' with an opaque keyset cursor. Why: a session starting meanwhile never shifts or repeats rows; a cursor stays valid across a restart.

Listed: every session of the project that ran a task, spent money or works now, planning calls included; not the conversation, not sessions without a project, not a session that ended without running a task and without spending. Why: every CHF a session spent is in exactly one row; automatic starts that found nothing (design section 4.8) are not news.

Chat is one line under the list, 'Chat about this project: CHF 0.30.' with Open Chat, only when above zero. Why: chat is one conversation, not sessions (§3.9), but its spend about the project must be visible (D3 lets it grow).

One figure per session, read when it is shown: the cost ledger's CHF sum for the session as booked, used by the list row, by SessionView.spent (the session page's 'Spent of this session's budget') and by the result's cost sentence, which the session page and the Overview's Last result render at read time through one function resultTextNow(stored text, stored outcome, ledger sum) in session-list.ts: the stored cost sentence, rebuilt from the stored outcome.spentChfMicro with result.ts's own cost builder, is replaced by the one for the ledger's sum; a stored text without that exact sentence (rows from before run C) is shown as stored, with the ledger's figure beside it. No stored text is ever rewritten, and executor.ts is not touched. An Update or a notification already sent keeps the amount it said: it is news of that moment (ADR 0116 says so). Why: ADR 0008 and U-074 (what the person reads is CHF from the ledger's own conversion); a rate change or a stopped run's late booking (R-lateusage) never leaves two amounts on one screen; editing stored text after the fact is fragile.

Credential words: 'CHF 0.80 on your API key', 'CHF 0.80 of your Claude subscription's allowance', 'CHF 0.80 of your plan credits', 'CHF 0.80 on your API key and your Claude subscription' when both paid; no credential words on the stand-in; moneyWords for amounts under a centime. Why: Settings measures a subscription against its allowance in CHF of API-equivalent use; 'on your subscription' would read as a charge.

The record: at its end each session writes handoff.outcome (the named LastSessionOutcome: done, failed with reasons, needs_you, paused with limit words, cancelled, released) on its own row, from the runner and from recovery; a planning call writes handoff.planning (its failure words, through redact and withoutIds) when it closes; the plan's size and fate are read from the plan card whose session_id is the row's. Rows from before run C fall back to handoff.done and handoff.blocked ('2 left for you'). Why: the list must read the same after a restart and after later sessions, without re-deriving it from logs.

How it ended: one map, the session page's (sessionStatusText/endedStatusText), with past tense for an ended session's two present-tense states ('Stopped to wait for a Claude credential', 'Ended with a plan for you to approve'); 'Ended: 1 task needs you' stays true now. A planning row says how it ended only when stopped, interrupted or failed; its page reads 'Drafting the plan', 'Plan drafted', 'Planning failed'. Why: §5 rule 4 true now; one map for the badge and the row.
An interrupted session's duration ends at its last logged event before the recovery's own session.ended line. Why: the downtime is not the session's length.

The session page gains 'Tasks in this session' (title opening the drawer, what happened here, 'now: …' when different, CHF this session spent on it) and 'All sessions'; GET /sessions/:id/tasks serves it. Why: the owner's 'each opening the session's page', with its tasks and log; U-086.

Routes: GET /projects/:id/sessions and GET /sessions/:id/tasks are new; GET /sessions keeps its shape (summary words for planning rows, spend as the one figure). All words are the daemon's. Why: the running poller and the phone use GET /sessions; a project route fits wave 8's ownership middleware; ADR 0102 (the phone shows the daemon's words).

startedBy words read who asked first, then the trigger: startedByWords(row) reads row.plan.startedBy ({by: 'person' | 'schedule' | 'hands_off' | 'continuation', continues?: the session it continues}, the shape fixed in the run C plan and written on the session row's plan JSON by d1109-starts-engine in sub-run C3; this area's tests seed a row that carries it through the store) and falls back to the trigger for rows without it. Words this area writes: 'started on its schedule' (by 'schedule', or trigger schedule), 'started from your phone' (by 'person' with trigger remote, or trigger remote), and, for rows made before run C, 'started by a pull request comment' (pr_comment) and 'started by CI' (ci), which d1109-starts-engine's S-4 stops producing; a plain Start or any other start by 'person', an answer's, Continue's or a limit change's start (trigger 'message') and the old credential wake (budget_reset) say nothing. d1109-starts-engine adds, in this same function only, the words for 'hands_off' and for 'continuation', which names the session it continues ('goes on with your session of 14:05': the owner's decision of 2026-11-09 that a session the person started goes on by itself when its Claude credential is back); a continuation is its own row. Why: keyed on the trigger, 'started by itself' would be untrue for a Continue or an answer; D6 owns who starts a session; the field's shape is fixed in the plan, so this area reads it before C3 writes it.

decisions: One identity for a link (new packages/runtime/src/sources/repository-use.ts): identityOf(entry) -> keys from parseRepoLocator/repoKey (host-checked, lower-case, every spelling) and folderKey (real path, lower-case on Windows), a folder's git root and its origin's repository key (read from .git and .git/config as files), and GitHub's repository id when read; projectsUsing(store, identity) over active projects, a joined project counting as the one it joined (settings.joined_from of the kept project, written by d1109-onerepo-join; read here) and a removed project (archived by Undo of its creation) using nothing; projectIdsOf(project) = [id, ...joined_from]. Why: discovery's keys already cover every spelling (ADR 0056 point 3); one function means New project, chat, Sources, import and W15-01 agree. Validation rule 5: a folder on another drive is another link (D:\Code\Site is not C:\Code\Site), a long path compares by its real path, and 'one folder inside the other' counts only when the inner folder has no git root of its own below the linked one: with C:\Code linked, C:\Code\notes is that project's but C:\Code\shop with its own .git is its own link, so a broad linked parent folder never swallows the repositories inside it.

The check runs before anything is written, at the one creation path (createProjectRecord: POST /projects, Sources' accept, the chat's port) and in project.create's plan and run (a new repositoryUse port in packages/commands/src/types.ts, so chat is refused before a read-back), and in importGitHubRepo. Refusal: ForerunnerError 'validation', HTTP 409, details {cause: 'repository_in_use', projectId, projectName} (the UI's buttons use the id; the person never sees it). Why: one gate, no row, no change-log row, no docs pull request for a refused link. The index reads every project row that is not archived (archived rows only to tell a joined project from a removed one), bounded like discovery (MAX_PROJECTS = 10,000, discovery.ts:123; above it the check refuses in words), never a silent limit such as project.active({limit: 100}) at server.ts:880.

The words (design section 5): 'o/site is already the project "Site". Open it, or add this to it as new work.'; for a folder 'This folder is already used by the project "Site". Open it, or add this to it as new work.' Buttons (at most three words, design section 5 rule 1): Open it, Add to it (only with a brief or goal), Cancel. Chat gets the same sentence as the tool's answer; project.create's definition says to offer that project (project.switch). Why: the owner's 'in an intelligent way': the person is led to the project that exists, from every entry point.

Add to plans only the new work: POST /projects/:id/intake {brief} (exists). For a project that already has tasks the intake runs in its plan-only form: its system prompt's section starts 'A project that already has work gets a new brief. Turn it into the tasks it adds and the order to do them in; write no documents.' in place of 'A new project has a brief.', the reply's shape has no docs, and no doc set, decision file or docs pull request is written for it; its user message gains a quoted block 'Already in the project (data, between the markers):' with each task as '- "<title>" (<status in words>)', at most 40 then 'and N more', and the instructions one line 'Plan only work that is not already in the project.'; milestones follow the project's mode as for any plan (small-project mode joins its open milestone, project-plan.ts:452-470; otherwise new milestones follow the existing ones), so no line promises a milestone of its own. An open plan card answers 'A plan for "Site" waits for your answer. Answer it first.' (no id). Why: a bigger project with parts is one project; the doc set belongs to a project's first plan, and a second 0001 decision and a second docs pull request would be untrue.

From the repository itself, read what exists today and what wave 8 keeps: .forerunner/project.json on the default branch (getFile) and the marks of its pull requests (project= in the hidden mark, fr/intake-<id>-docs branch names, the L-16 visible line 'Forerunner project <id>.'): the open ones name the project when there is no marker, and every one, open, merged or closed, counts for its activity (listPullRequests with state 'all' and an append-only sort option 'updated' (GitHub's sort=updated, direction desc), its first page of 100), so a project whose pull requests are merged within a day still shows as used; a push straight to the default branch without a pull request is not seen (Forerunner's own work always goes through pull requests; ADR 0117 names the limit). A project id there that is not a row on this install (any status), nor joined into or taken over by a project here, is a project that is not on this computer. Run C writes nothing new into repositories. Why: the marker is wave 8's status issue key K; the marks exist since W15-01/W15-08; a new file would cost every repository a docs pull request. Their activity is a fact read with them: PullRequestInfo gains updatedAt and authorLogin (append-only; github.ts's pull request mapping, the memory host, testenv's fake host), and the install's own login comes from the host's whoAmI.

A project that is not on this computer (another person's Forerunner on their own PC, or the person's own earlier install: release checklist step 1 removes the old install and installs fresh on the same PC, so 'on another computer' would be untrue; design section 5 rule 4) is never a second project here and never taken over while someone uses it (D9, the owner's answer 1 of 2026-11-09). When the repository names exactly one such project (its marker, else the one project id its open pull requests' marks carry), the offer is to work on it together, always first: it writes nothing and fits every case, the person's own reinstall and their own second computer included. Take it over is offered second, and only when no pull request carrying one of its marks (open, merged or closed) was updated by another GitHub account within the last 14 days (ACTIVE_ELSEWHERE_DAYS; this install's own login does not block it: the person's own earlier install, or their own second computer, whose consequence line tells them to choose it only when no Forerunner uses that project now): 'o/kite is already the Forerunner project "Kite club", which is not on this computer; last active on GitHub on 3 Nov. Work on it together, or take it over if nobody works on it any more.' with Work together, Take it over and Cancel (the activity part reads '..., from your account' for this install's own login and is left out when no pull request carries a mark). When a pull request carrying one of its marks (open, merged or closed) was updated by another GitHub account within the last 14 days: 'o/kite is already the Forerunner project "Kite club"; another GitHub account worked on it on 8 Nov. One repository is one project, so work on it together here.' with Work together and Cancel (no take-over). Consequence lines (at most 100 characters): Work together 'This Forerunner works on "Kite club" too; nothing on GitHub changes now.' (with a brief or goal: 'Works on "Kite club" too and plans your brief as its new work.'); Take it over 'The repository then names this project: choose it only if no Forerunner uses "Kite club" now.' (its Details: 'The pull requests of "Kite club" stay as they are.'). No name known: 'another Forerunner project'. Two or more unknown ids and no marker: 'other Forerunner projects', with Take it over (no other account active within 14 days) and Cancel, never Work together (which project it is cannot be told). POST /projects with together {project: <the id the refusal named>} creates the together project (the Work together decision); with takeOver {projects: <the ids the refusal named>} creates the project with settings.took_over {projects, name, at}; a together or takeOver that does not name exactly what the repository shows now is refused again, and a takeOver while another account was active within 14 days is refused. Refusal details carry canWorkTogether and canTakeOver. Why: Work together comes first because it writes nothing and cannot break a project someone still uses (a take-over replaces the marker); the owner's answer 1: each person runs their own Forerunner with their own credentials, and two of them on one repository are one project ('work seamlessly in the same git'); a project someone else uses is never taken over; a project nobody uses any more, or the person's own earlier install, can be (today's 14-day rule, kept as the measure of 'nobody uses it any more'); the person decides with facts (the date and whose account), nothing is guessed; forerunner-sandbox's marker names a deleted bench's 'Kite club'.

Take-over effects: the project's next docs pull request (the intake's set on its own branch, or the scaffold) replaces a marker that names one of the taken-over ids (writeInstallMarker gains replace: <ids>; any other project's marker is still never overwritten) and its body says 'This repository was the Forerunner project "Kite club"; it is now "<name>"'s.' Nothing of the other project is pushed to, commented on, closed or listed (W15-01); while its status pull request is open this project's status stays in the app with D1-9's words. Why: the repository then tells every computer which project it is. A together project never takes over and never replaces a marker (it writes none).

Marker cases: with no marker and pull request marks naming unknown ids, the take-over records them all, so none of them refuses again; a marker naming a project removed on this install (archived by Undo of its creation) frees the repository: the creation records took_over {projects: [that id], removed: true} without an offer (the removed project was this person's own), so its first docs pull request replaces the marker and the stricter legacy rule below does not leave the new project's unmarked docs pull requests to nobody. Why: the adversarial check's two open cases; one rule ('replace only a took_over id') covers both. A removed together project (archived by Undo of its creation) never frees the repository: its id is the other Forerunner's project too, so the rule above applies only to a project that was never together, and Work together brings that row back (the Work together decision).

An existing project whose copy's marker (this computer's copy of the default branch, read as a file) names a project that is not on this computer gets one Overview line 'o/kite is also the Forerunner project "Kite club", which is not on this computer.' with Take it over when no pull request of it (open, merged or closed) was updated by another account within 14 days (else the line adds 'another GitHub account worked on it on 8 Nov' and has no button in this area), with the offer's consequence line; no card. d1109-onerepo-join (C4, OJ-11) adds Work together to this line, before Take it over: this project's work moves into a together project of that id, so the project here becomes the repository's project without a take-over. Take it over runs the new command repo.take_over: medium risk for every actor (read back with Yes and No from chat; the press is the yes in the app), refused for an agent actor ('Only you can take over a repository.'), reversible until its docs pull request exists: its undoBlocked answers 'Its pull request on GitHub already names this project: close it there first.' while that pull request is open and 'The repository already names this project on GitHub, so this cannot be undone here.' once it merged; before that, Undo removes took_over and the Overview line comes back. Covers projects made before the rule and creations made while GitHub could not be read. Why: visible, not blocking; the person decides; a take-over replaces another project's file through a pull request, so no agent does it and no Undo promises what it cannot take back.

GitHub unreachable, no token or the repository unreadable at creation: the local check still runs; the repository check is skipped without a word at creation (it cannot know) and the Overview line above appears once the copy shows another marker. Why: never block creating on GitHub's answer; never claim what was not read. ADR 0117 names this as the one place the rule fails open, and why.

W15-01's legacy rule, simplified: soleLinkedProject and its comparator and per-call scan go; the docs paths and the daemon's docs rows ask the index: an unmarked status or scaffold pull request is this project's only when it is the one project on this install using the repository (joined ones count as it, removed ones as others: fail closed as before) and this computer's copy's marker names no other project (new, stricter), and it is not a together project (a together project is never 'the one project here': the repository is the other Forerunner's project too). isProjectDocsPr/isProjectStatusPr read projectIdsOf (a joined project's mark and intake branch are the kept project's). Why: the task asks to simplify where the rule makes it moot without weakening it; a legacy pair now has an end (d1109-onerepo-join).

The Docs row of a status kept in the app because another project's status pull request is open: 'Kept in the app while "A"'s status pull request is open on GitHub.' (a project that is not on this computer: 'while another project's status pull request is open on GitHub; close it there to have this one's there.'). Why: D1-9; the words of the setting-off case stay.

A URL on a git host this install does not use is refused at link: 'Forerunner works with repositories on github.com, not gitlab.com. Link a GitHub repository or a folder.' Why: today it is silently linked as GitHub's repository of the same owner and name.

Renamed or transferred repositories: RepoInfo gains id (GitHub's numeric id; github.ts toRepo, MemoryGitHost, the fake host); the check reads the id of the new link and of the projects here linked to repositories on the same host (at most 20 reads, kept in memory for the daemon's life; unreadable -> keys only); the marker, when merged, already names the project whatever the repository's name. Why: GitHub redirects an old name, so two names can be one repository.

Security: the marker and pull request bodies are repository content: parsed strictly (marker schema 1, a URI-encoded mark), a name cut at 60 characters with control characters removed, passed through the injection scan (flagged -> 'another Forerunner project'), shown in quotes, and in chat only inside the tool's answer as quoted data, never in a model's instructions; folder identity reads files only, no git process in the person's folder; GitHub reads use the configured host and token, never the page reader. Why: the rules for every design. A command answer that quotes such text (project.create's and repo.take_over's 'already the Forerunner project ...' refusal with the marker's name) carries the untrusted mark (d1109-chat-guard's CommandOutcome.untrusted), so the hooks wrap and scan it and every later change of that chat turn is read back. Work together adopts an id read from the repository at the press (marker schema 1: a UUID), never one from the model, the page or the request body beyond matching it; that id never names a row of this install other than a removed together project; the marker's name stays data (cut, scanned, quoted).

Two people, one repository (D9, the owner's answer 1 of 2026-11-09): every person runs their own Forerunner on their own PC with their own API key and subscription; no shared database or server is needed; two Forerunners on one repository are one project and meet on GitHub. Run C builds the recognition (the decisions on reading the repository, on a project that is not on this computer and on an existing project's line: the repository's marker and pull request marks, with their activity) and the same-project link (the Work together decision: this Forerunner adopts the repository's project id; nothing is taken over and nothing is written into the other Forerunner's pull requests), with words that promise only what exists: each Forerunner keeps its own tasks, cards and sessions; what the other does shows in its pull requests and in the shared git history; each merges its own pull requests. Wave 8 (re-planned: /tmp/frbench/wave8-replan-brief.md) builds seeing each other's work through the pinned status issue (one comment per Forerunner), claims (work one Forerunner announces that the other's planner and runner leave out) and the repository guide (AGENTS.md: 'link this repository in your own Forerunner and choose Work together'). Why: no promise the code does not keep (design section 5 rule 9); the owner's 'seamlessly in the same git' comes in two steps: run C makes it one project, wave 8 makes the two see each other.

Work together (D9; OR-15): POST /projects with together {project} (with the brief, goal and link as typed) creates this Forerunner's project with the id the repository names, read again from the repository at the press (marker schema 1: a UUID; never an id the model or the page supplies), named as the marker names it (cut at 60 characters, control characters removed, scanned; when flagged or missing, the name the person typed, else the dialog asks for one), with settings.together {name, at, activeOn, login} (activeOn: the last activity the offer named). Refused in words, nothing written: the id is a row on this install other than a removed together project ('o/kite is already the project "Kite club". Open it.'); the repository now names another project or none; the link is a folder ('Work together needs the GitHub repository: link o/kite, not a folder.'); GitHub cannot be read at the press ('GitHub did not answer, so the project cannot be checked. Try again.': Work together needs the id from GitHub, so it does not fail open as creation does). A removed together project is brought back by Work together (the same row, its tasks as they were). What a together project does differently, and only this: it writes nothing to the repository by itself (no marker, no scaffold, no doc set, no docs pull request, no status pull request: the repository's documents and marker are the other Forerunner's); isProjectDocsPr and isProjectStatusPr answer false for every way a pull request names its own id, since those are the other Forerunner's: the intake branch fr/intake-<its id>-docs (docs.ts matches that branch by the project id today, :179-180), the hidden mark, the L-16 visible line 'Forerunner project <its id>.' and a recorded scaffold pr_url (it records none); an unmarked status or scaffold pull request is never its own (never sole-linked, decision 10); those of an id in its joined_from (OJ-11) are listed as information only, never written to, merged or rebuilt (the together rule wins over joined_from); its first plan, and every brief after, uses the Add to decision's plan-only form, also with no tasks here yet; its task pull requests carry its project mark and their own task marks as today, and a pull request is this Forerunner's only through its own task rows (branch or pr_url), its take-outs or a docs branch of an id it joined, so neither Forerunner lists, pushes to, comments on, merges, closes or rebuilds the other's pull requests (pull-requests.ts, the merge loop, the take-out and conflict notices and the GitHub watcher already read task rows: the composed two-home case proves it); its Docs status row reads 'Kept in the app: you work on "Kite club" together, so GitHub's copy is left as it is.' (true whether or not the Forerunner that made it still runs). Its Overview line: 'Shared on GitHub with another Forerunner: each keeps its own tasks.' (Details: 'What the other Forerunner does shows in its pull requests on GitHub; each of you merges your own.'). Undo of its creation archives it as for any project (nothing on GitHub to take back). In chat, project.create gains together: true (no id: the daemon reads the repository's project at run time), medium risk, read back once ('Work on "Kite club" together: this Forerunner joins it as the same project. Nothing on GitHub changes now.' [Yes] [No]); the refusal's tool answer ends 'Say "work on it together" to join it here.'. Why: the owner's answer 1 ('nothing is taken over; nothing is written into the other person's pull requests'); with one project id on two Forerunners, a docs or status pull request marked with it would otherwise be taken as each one's own.
