areas.title: The agent keeps its task list right during a run: one check on evidence between tasks (a report's 'For the task list:' lines, a review note, notes left from before), on the planning model and booked in the session; five kinds of change through the registry (wording, split, a missing step, order, a duplicate dropped), fenced in code; from Standard each made and told with one Undo, at Advisor and Assisted suggested on one card; added work joins the session only if it fits, else waits for the next Start; never a running task, a budget or another project; never steered by a report
problems: [major] D7-1: After the plan is approved the agent never corrects its own task list: a task a specialist finds is two jobs, a missing step, a wrong order or a duplicate stays as planned; the person edits each task by hand or redrafts the whole plan. Owner's words: "if I say set this up and I approve a plan and then it adds a bunch of tasks, I want it to be able to fix its tasks. Like as part of a run, it should be able to do things like that." Where: session/runner.ts:1379-1476 (replan only takes tasks that became ready), :3825-3858 (StaticPlanner, no model call), daemon/compose.ts:2675.

[major] D7-2: A specialist that finds its task too big, a step missing or a wrong order has nowhere to say so that anything reads; rung 2 of the ladder asks it to 'say in the report what should be split off' and nothing reads it, and the ladder's split is not built (only 'change specialist'). Owner's words: "I want it to be able to fix its tasks." Where: session/executor.ts:640-641, :784-800 (ladderStandIn), :1013 (the report's only headings), models/ladder.ts:305.

[major] D7-4: The autonomy level cannot decide when the agent asks first about its tasks: creating or editing tasks is 'non_routine', free only from Trusted, and no class covers the agent's own fixes. Owner's words: "The agent changing its own tasks with the autonomy level deciding when it asks first. That's also good." Where: enforcement/autonomy.ts:36-49, :64-74.

[major] D7-3a: The task commands cannot express the fixes: no split, no 'add a step before X', no 'drop as a duplicate'; cancel is always medium risk. Owner's words: "I want it to be able to fix its tasks." Where: packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:835-950 (task.create), :960-1027 (task.transition, :965), types.ts:33-60 (COMMAND_NAMES).

[minor] D7-6: Each change an agent makes posts its own Inbox Update; ten fixes would be ten Updates, against design §3.8's one line per session. Owner's words: none on this point (the owner's 'We don't need notifications like that' is about a status line for waiting work); the rule is design §3.8's 'What becomes an Update: one line per session'. Where: packages/commands/src/executor.ts:684-699; session/runner.ts:3011-3027.

[minor] D7-6b: The change log has no channel for a session's own change: an agent's change in a run could only be stored as 'api' and reads 'In the app' on Changes. Owner's words: "each change shown with one Undo" (confirmed D7). Where: state/src/types.ts:111, state/src/schema.ts:499, apps/ui/src/pages/ChangesPage.tsx:56-61.

[major, security] D7-8: Nothing would keep a report from steering the plan once the agent may change tasks: reports are screened only for lessons, and no injection case covers a report. Owner's words (the rule for every design): text from cards, chat, pages or files never becomes instructions to a model. Where: session/runner.ts:2866-2890 (the only screen of report content), evals/src/injection-runner.ts:95 (web and email only).

[major, security] D7-8b: A task the agent adds from a report could name any runnable specialist at Standard, the researcher included, which reads web pages; the report's text would reach that specialist's brief through the planning model, with only the heuristic scan in between; Owner's words (the rule for every design): text from cards, chat, pages or files never becomes instructions to a model; Where: evals/registry/specialists/researcher/specialist.md, science-evaluator/specialist.md (cc:WebFetch, cc:WebSearch); session/executor.ts (the brief from the task row).
decisions: The check runs on evidence only (a report's 'For the task list:' lines, a review note the task did not cause, notes kept from before), at most once per task boundary and three times a session, never after the wrap-up line. Why: cost; the owner wants fixes 'as part of a run', not a paid replan after every task.

The planning model at one effort step below the intake (medium), 4,096 output tokens, 120 s, a JSON reply and no tools, routed like the intake's planning call, capped at its own estimate inside the session's work budget, a Run row 'task-check' booked in the session. Why: planning quality for a small call; one path on both credentials; money visible and inside the budget.

Five kinds of change, each a registry command (task.update, task.dependencies, task.create with 'then', task.split, task.transition with 'duplicate_of'). Why: every change gets the change log, the version check and a state-based Undo that survives a restart (ADR 0030); no new write path to the store.

A split keeps the task as its first part and adds 1 to 3 new tasks; every criterion goes word for word into a part; a task's own budget is shared, never raised. Why: the folder, branch and earlier work stay; the bar cannot be lowered by splitting; no budget is passed.

New action class plan_fix, free from Standard up (Standard, Trusted, Autopilot); Advisor and Assisted get one suggestion card. Why: the owner confirmed on 2026-11-09 that the agent changes its own tasks without asking from Standard up and asks first at Advisor and Assisted on one card (the autonomy level deciding when it asks first); plan_fix frees only the bounded fixes.

Ask first at every level for flagged input, the person's own task, a criterion removed from a task that ran or has open findings, a deploy or migration step, a question for the person, a new task whose specialist reaches further than its source task's, more than two drops, or an unlike duplicate. Why: these are the changes whose mistake costs the person (their edit lost, the bar lowered, risky work or their time added, work cancelled).

Each change the agent makes alone is one Changes row (source 'session') with one Undo, a line on the session page and no Inbox line; the session's one Update counts them. A set the person approves with one Yes is one row with one Undo. Why: the confirmed 'every change shown with one Undo' and design §3.8's 'What becomes an Update: one line per session'.

Added work joins the running session only by d1109-starts-engine's admit rule: the parts of a split promised task share its remaining estimate, a new task or a step before a promised task joins only if the room after the promise and what joined covers it (else both wait for the next Start, named once), and the check itself is paid only from that room; the agent's preparation never starts a session, the hands-off setting included. Why: D6 (the person says when a session starts) and option C ('the session keeps its promise').

A task with an open card (failed after its tries, needs your answer, paused at a budget) or paused by the person is left alone. Why: the card is the one place for that decision (design §3.8); D4's continuation stays as built.

Evidence goes in the data envelope and is scanned; a flagged line is kept, never sent to the model, and turns the set into a suggestion card that quotes it; a new task's specialist reaches no further than its source task's without a yes; a task written from a report says so in its brief; the strict schema and the fence hold whatever the model returns; the check's run has no tools. Why: a prompt may ask, only code can allow (AGENTS.md); a report must not reach the web through a task it wrote.

areas.title: One credential policy the engine follows: five presets read at every pick by every call (tasks, reviews, planning, the task check, chat, background jobs), an explicit earlier choice read as the policy until one is chosen, and with no choice ever made the default preset (subscription first, then wait) for every call, with no separate order for chat, planning or reviews; a usage limit, the subscription's share, a key's monthly cap and a refusal are stops; next goes on at once (the stopped task finished from its kept work), ask files one card per stop whose yes is a grant for that stop and the person's start of the waiting session, wait moves nothing until the stop ends, when a session the person started that waited goes on by itself on the credential that is back (d1109-starts-engine's continuation, the owner's decision of 2026-11-09); a refusal informs once and is never retried; every switch recorded with its cost

decisions: CE-1 One policy: human.notify_prefs.credential_policy, one of subscription_then_wait, subscription_then_ask, subscription_then_key, key_then_subscription, key_only (packages/billing/src/policy.ts: CREDENTIAL_POLICIES; ruleOf(id) = {order, whenStopped: next | ask | wait, kinds}, key_only without the subscription; credentialPolicyOf(prefs) = the stored id, else derived at every read: billing_order with the subscription first + wait or unset -> subscription_then_wait, + use_other -> subscription_then_key, api_key or plan_credits first + use_other -> key_then_subscription, + wait or unset -> {chosen: 'earlier', the stored order, whenStopped wait, both kinds: the chooser keeps running a task only the subscription can do here on it, as today, which key_only would not}, no billing_order -> the default preset subscription_then_wait for every call and every purpose ({chosen: false}, so Settings shows it as used until the person picks), or subscription_then_key under an explicit mid_session_limit use_other; CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER, the routed provider's fallbackOrder and every other per-call order go: one order for tasks, chat, planning, reviews, the task check and the background jobs (the chooser's capability moves stay, said on the plan card, ADR 0100 point 13); stopKeyOf(source, status); moneyRank, the earlier choice ranked as key_only). Why: the owner's 'a framework for what to use when, and then the system just does it'; read at every pick, so a change applies to the next call; deriving at read changes nothing a person chose (an explicit earlier choice is kept as it was chosen), and a person who never chose gets the default preset for everything, not a hidden split (the owner's answer 4 of 2026-11-09: 'it should use the order that the user specifies ... There should be a nice clean options menu'; ADR 0100 point 2 amended).

CE-2 The router holds every stop: RouteContext.whenStopped replaces waitOnRest (waitOnRest still read as 'wait' for one release); the held list covers resting (reason limit), refused, plan_share (share, until the next month's start UTC) and monthly_limit (key_month), each with until and stopKey; under ask and wait a held first choice throws unavailable with details.waitFor {sourceId, kind, reason, until, stopKey, ask}; a grant {to, stopKey} on the held source whose stopKey is the current one lets the granted kind serve; a grant never lifts the hold for purpose batch (background jobs); next moves as today; RouteContext.heldNow (sources the caller saw stop on this call) are held like resting ones. Why: one place decides, so every caller agrees (7a, 7b, 7c).

CE-3 RouterTaskBilling.pick reads the policy at every pick for every purpose (session, critic, interactive, which D7's task check uses, chat, batch; a grant covers every purpose but batch); the sources in req.exclude go to the router as heldNow, not as withheld, under ask and wait; at a stop it never moves to a lower chooser group: the task waits with reason needs. The agent's task check (d1109-selftasks-run's runTaskCheck, merged in C4) is held like planning: under wait or an unanswered ask it makes no call, books nothing, keeps its notes for the next boundary or session and returns held with the wait (this area's one branch in task-check.ts); under ask its hold ensures the one ask card (CE-7). Why: one rule for every call; the exclude list today hides the very stop the hold must see; the plan card's 'only it can' stays true (ADR 0100 point 13).

CE-4 RoutedProvider follows the rule and has no order of its own (its fallbackOrder, CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER, goes: the policy's order for every call): after rest or refuse it picks again under the rule; under ask and wait the call ends with the wait (code unavailable, details.wait), which each caller handles as today: the critic's review waits in review without a counted try (review-refusal.ts), the plan waits (the intake's waitNow), chat holds (CE-9), a job skips (CE-10); under next one move as today, recorded with its cost (CE-11). holdNow(model) beside waitNow says whether a call would be held and whether a one-off switch could serve (for chat and d1109-chat-depth's thorough pass). Why: D5-1 is the main money leak today.

CE-5 A task its credential stopped keeps its work; under next, or after a grant, it goes back to the head of the session's queue and continues on the next credential in the same session; the brief's previous-run section for a usage_limit, credential_refused or share-stopped run is a sibling of whereTheLastRunStopped with exact text ('stopped when its Claude credential reached its limit' / 'was refused' / 'reached the share of the subscription Forerunner may use'), never 'It failed', with its siblings for a run that changed no file ('The last run of this task stopped when its Claude credential reached its limit, before it changed any file.') and for one that left no note ('It left no note: its Claude credential stopped it before it could write one.'); under ask and wait it waits, the session goes on with what can run and ends to wait, and at the stop's end that session goes on by itself as the person's own start (d1109-starts-engine S-10's continuation: the rest of its promise and budget, on the credential that is back, never another one unless the rule is next or a grant of this stop covers it), while work outside a session the person started is ready for the person's next Start. Why: 7a ('the task to be completed by the API') without spending twice.

CE-6 Forerunner's share reached mid-run (the hooks' plan level, unchanged) returns as a credential stop with reason share and its handoff kept on the run (read by CE-5's brief): no budget card, the session does not end for it, the rule decides; the stop ends at the month's start or when the person raises the allowance (the share falls under the cap; the stop key changes); then a person's session that waited for it goes on by itself (d1109-starts-engine S-10's continuation, on the subscription) and other waiting work reads Ready for the next Start; nothing else starts (d1109-starts-engine S-3, S-10). The raise's change line is this area's (it replaces S-3's line for the allowance): with a person's session waiting on the share 'Your subscription's allowance is raised: your session of 14:05 goes on now.' (inside quiet hours '... goes on at 07:00, after your quiet hours.'), otherwise 'Your subscription's allowance is raised: 2 tasks are ready again for your next Start.'. The ask card's Wait line for the share has CE-7's two forms: 'Nothing moves until Tue 1 Dec, 01:00, or until you raise the allowance; then your session goes on.' while the person's session waits, else 'Nothing moves. After Tue 1 Dec, 01:00, or a raised allowance, the work runs at your next Start.' (the month's start UTC shown in the person's time zone). Budget cards at source 'plan' filed before the upgrade keep their wake (wakeBudgetWaits). Why: one behaviour per stop; a raised allowance must end the wait (U-052); no limit passed.

CE-7 Ask first: one card per stop (key credential:ask), filed only by the writer that set limits.asking {stopKey, requestId} with the version check, only when work needs it (a task run, a review, planning, the task check; not chat alone, not a job), the other credential can serve now and the caps have room for the waiting work's next call; its words from credential-words.ts, computed when shown. 'Use API key' re-reads the stop, writes limits.grant {to, stopKey, by: 'card', at} (version-checked; audit billing.grant), then: the waiting tasks of a session that still runs go back into it as its own tasks (d1109-starts-engine's readmit on the admit handle, which clears the runner's notAgain for them), a session that ended to wait goes on now as the person's start (personContinue: by 'person', the rest of its promise, its cap less what the ledger booked), a waiting plan is drafted, work outside a person's session stays ready for the next Start. The grant covers every project's tasks, their reviews and planning, the task check and chat until the stop ends (the owner's answer 3: 'For all work.'); Forerunner's own monthly checks (the model watch and the critic's check on known examples, CE-10) are not the person's work and wait for the first choice at no cost; the option's consequence line says what the yes covers ('Your work and chat use your API key until 15:40: about CHF 0.90 for what waits now.') and the card's Details says the rest once ('Forerunner's own monthly checks wait for your subscription; they cost nothing meanwhile.'). 'Wait' closes the card and moves nothing until the stop ends; then the person's waiting session goes on by itself on the first choice (its continuation stays kept: 'Nothing moves until 15:40; then your session goes on with your subscription.'), and work outside a person's session is ready for the next Start ('Nothing moves. After 15:40 the work runs at your next Start.' when no session of the person waits); the asking mark keeps the stop, so no second card comes; the time a Wait line names is when the session goes on: the stop's end, or the end of the person's quiet hours when that is later (d1109-starts-engine S-10); recordWait(source, stopKey) records the same answer without a card, for the Start dialog's 'Start at 15:40' under ask (d1109-cred-screens), so no card follows the person's own choice. A second or late answer changes nothing and returns the card's Done line; an answer after the stop ended grants nothing. The wake, before takeReady, ends grants whose stop is over and withdraws open cards whose stop ended (then the waiting session goes on as after Wait), whose other credential cannot serve any more, or whose preset changed. Why: 'after asking human' as one card; answered once; restart-safe; no start the person did not ask for (D6).

CE-8 A refusal follows the rule and always informs: one card per refusal at a time, filed only by the writer that flips limits.refusedCard {refusedAt, open} to open with the version check (refuse() and noteWait's TR-10 path alike: concurrent refusals file one, and work that waits on the still-refused credential after the card was closed files it once more); closing the card clears open; refusalWhyOf(error) stores a category (expired sign-in, invalid or deleted key, not allowed for this model or workspace, other), never the provider's text; the card's body says what the work does under the rule (wait, next, or ask with Use API key / Wait, staying open as the fix-it card after an answer); a refused credential gets no second request from any path (a switch, a grant, a continuation, a late answer, chat, a job, the probe) until a different one is saved. Why: 7c; no retry that could lock the person's account.

CE-9 Chat asks holdNow before its model path; held: no model call and no ledger row, the hold reply written by code, with a per-turn 'Use API key' when the other credential serves now and the caps have room (the reply view's oneOff {label, explain}; the press runs that one question again with allowSwitch on that request only: no grant, no card; the route's flag for the press is d1109-cred-screens'); a standing grant or next: chat answers on the other credential and the reply's note says so once per stop per conversation; 'I could not answer (' never appears for a credential wait. Why: chat spends too (7b); the smallest consent; the person is in the chat. Under the default preset (nothing chosen) chat answers on the subscription too (one order, the owner's answer 4), so at the subscription's limit under its wait chat holds as above, with the one-off press; d1109-chat-depth's ask line, hand-over step, footer, setting row and Think it through then use their Claude-plan forms (the amounts at API prices, 'on your Claude plan'; built here if C3 left that wording in not_done); a longer pass that goes ahead without asking runs on the credential the policy serves chat now, and the ask line names that credential when it is not the person's first (d1109-chat-depth's first-credential check is replaced by this).

CE-10 Background jobs (batch: the model watch and its evals, the monthly calibration) never ask and never switch under ask or wait, a standing grant included: a held call spends nothing, files no card, logs one line, and the job is not marked done for its period, so the first tick after the stop runs it. Why: no card and no money for work nobody started.

CE-11 Switch data: the run row's artifacts carry switchedFrom {kind, stop}; the session log gets billing.switch {taskId, from, to, stop, until} once per stop and billing.back once when the first choice serves again; SessionResult.switched [{taskId, from, to, usdMicro}] summed from the ledger; CostView.byCredential (each billing source's spend in the view's window); RoutedProvider's fallback sentence in the person's time zone; the log lines from credential-words.ts. Why: every screen (d1109-cred-screens) reads data, not re-parsed sentences; 7a 'transparent'.

CE-12 One notification (credentialSwitched, normal urgency) per stop and session, only for a move onto money the policy made by itself inside a running session: not for a grant the person gave, not for a session whose Start dialog said it would run on the key, not for a move onto the subscription; deduplicated by limits.switchNotified {stopKey, sessionIds} (version-checked, restart-safe); none for a wait. Why: 7a and 7c ('notification or information'); the owner wants no notifications about waiting work.

CE-13 settings.set credential_policy: medium risk; narrows by moneyRank (subscription_then_wait 0, subscription_then_ask 1, subscription_then_key 2, key_then_subscription 3, key_only 3; not chosen counts as the preset it reads as: the default subscription_then_wait 0, or subscription_then_key 2 under an explicit use_other), so a narrowing acts at once and a widening asks the person's yes; an agent actor is refused; an Undo is judged the same way; the settings_set tool definition lists credential_policy with its five values and neither legacy key; settings.set billing_order or mid_session_limit once credential_policy is stored, and an Undo of their old rows, answer 'This was replaced by "Which Claude does the work"; change it there.'. Why: money settings never widen by text; a tool definition is model-facing code.
root_causes: packages/billing/src/router.ts: the 'wait' rule (waitOnRest) was built for task runs and two kinds of stop (a rest, a refusal); the share and the key's monthly cap stayed plain skips, so they move work onto the next credential under any setting.

packages/runtime/src/wiring/billing-pick.ts: the sources a caller saw stop on this call are withheld before the router (exclude), and the groups loop moves to a lower chooser group on any 'no source' that is not a hold.

packages/runtime/src/provider/routed.ts: the non-task calls have their own one-time move to the next source, outside the person's setting, and their own fallback order (CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER) for a person who chose none.

packages/runtime/src/session/billing.ts and packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts: an order and a mid-session rule as two settings with different reach per purpose; no value for asking and no state for an answer (asked, granted).
packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts and budget-pause.ts: the subscription's share is enforced as a money budget level and handled as a budget pause, not as the subscription running out.
packages/runtime/src/session/task-context.ts: a credential-stopped run is read as a failed attempt although its work is kept.
packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts, routed.ts and notifications/producers.ts: a switch is a log sentence only; no fact on the run, the session or the result, no producer.
packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts and billing-pick.ts refuse(): filing a card is not tied to the version-checked mark that decided it, and the card stores no reason.

(the figure: the calibration's monthly budget at the day's rate; design §5 rule 6: plain words, no 'verdict'; the owner's answer 6 of 2026-11-09 asked what it is for), their last task, review and stop events, the scheduler's waiting person starts and the person's sessions waiting to go on after a credential wait (the kept continuation on a wait entry, d1109-starts-engine S-10: state 'waiting', no stop choices, cancel true); GET /running answers it, a run.changed event carries it on the stream and in polling, and /health gains running {projectName, text} (append-only) while activeSessions stops counting a plan being drafted. The words: 'Quote page · the coder works on "Style the page"', '... · the critic checks "X"', '... · picks the next task', '... · plans the session', '... · wraps up "X" at its budget', '... · stops after "X"', '· then Garden site' for a waiting person start; 'Quote page · waiting until 15:40, then it goes on' for a person's session waiting for its Claude credential (the owner's words of 2026-11-09; 'Quote page · waiting for a new API key, then it goes on' after a refusal; when the person's quiet hours end later than the stop, their end: 'Quote page · waiting until 07:00 (after your quiet hours), then it goes on'; a wait for any other reason, such as the share or a key's monthly cap that d1109-cred-engine adds beside this area, the generic 'Quote page · waiting for Claude, then it goes on', which d1109-cred-screens words with its date in C6); each at most 80 characters with titles shortened. runText is exported so d1109-sessions' working row says the same words. Why: one place per fact (design §5 rule 10); the phone later shows the same words (ADR 0102); the shell needs it without the UI.

V-2 One element on every page: RunIndicator, a bar directly under the header (role status, a pulsing dot, the words, the elapsed time, Stop ▾) on every route and at every width, never inside the collapsed menu, replacing RunningChip and the header's Stop all button; Stop offers Stop after this task (POST /sessions/:id/pause), Stop now (POST /sessions/:id/stop, asked once) and Stop all (POST /kill, asked once, 'Stops every session; none starts until you allow it again.'); the text opens the session; the store keeps it from run.changed; document.title reads '● Quote page · Forerunner' while it runs. The stopped bar, the no-key bar and the palette's Stop all question stay. Why: the owner: 'very visually clear no matter where the person is'; 'no clutter': one consistent element instead of two. A waiting session's bar shows its words (V-1's, e.g. 'Quote page · waiting until 15:40, then it goes on') with Cancel in place of Stop, without the pulsing dot; Cancel's one-line explanation is 'Nothing starts when Claude is back; its tasks wait for your Start.' and it sends POST /projects/:id/continuation/cancel; document.title changes only while a session runs.

V-3 The same element elsewhere: Home's and the Overview's Working now render RunIndicator in its block form (same words, same Stop), and the project status line (project-status.ts, design §2) adds 'Waiting until 15:40 (your subscription's limit), then it goes on' with Cancel (the person's session waiting to go on), 'Starts at 15:40 (your subscription's limit)' with Cancel (a start kept for a reset, POST /projects/:id/continuation/cancel), 'Starts after your quiet hours' (a held hands-off start) and 'Starts after the session on "Quote page"' (a waiting person start), and rule 4 reads 'Ready: 3 tasks wait for your Start' with Continue. Why: design §3.2 and §3.4 keep Working now; the owner named 'Home, the project'; the project's one sentence says what waits and what will start.
V-4 Talk shows it: the conversation panel's first line is RunIndicator's compact form with Stop. Why: the modal covers the header.

V-5 The ended session's page says what comes next: a session that ended to wait for its credential with its continuation kept shows one block 'Waiting until 15:40 (your subscription's limit), then it goes on with "B" and 1 more.' with Cancel; after Cancel (or when no continuation is kept) 'Stopped to wait for your subscription's limit until 15:40: "B" and 1 more wait.' with Continue ('Opens Start with the rest of this session and the CHF 1.20 left of its budget.'); with a person start kept for the reset instead, 'Starts again at 15:40 with "B" and 1 more.' with Cancel. Why: the owner's decision of 2026-11-09 (the person's session goes on by itself, shown with Cancel); the person who opens that session can stop the wait or go on with what is left.

V-6 The Inbox's Done line offers Start when the answer prepared work and no session of that project runs (it opens that project's Start dialog); never while one runs. Why: the person's start is one click from where they answered, without a reminder.

V-7 The desktop shell: tray_view's tooltip starts with /health.running ('Quote page: the coder works on "A"'), the tray menu's first item shows the same words (disabled) while a session runs, 'Stop all sessions' and 'Allow sessions again' replace 'Kill switch: stop everything' and 'Resume' (the question 'Stop every running session now? No session starts until you allow it again.'), and the main window's title is 'Forerunner — Quote page is working' while one runs, 'Forerunner' otherwise. Why: a minimised window or the tray is where a person looks when the window is not on screen; design §5 plain words. While a person's session only waits to go on, the tooltip's first line and the menu's first item read 'Quote page: waiting until 15:40, then it goes on' and the title and the icon stay as when nothing runs (the dot and the title mean a session runs now).
V-8 The tray icon gets a blue dot while a session runs, drawn over the app's own icon at run time (no new asset). Why: the one signal visible without hovering, on Windows and Linux.
V-9 Docs and the bench walk with screenshots of every screen with and without a running session.

decisions: 'fix the tasks' (and its synonyms, English and German) is recognised by the parser without a model call; the chat model gets one fix_tasks tool for the same request in other words. Why: no fast-model call before a planning-model call; one path.

The check, the fence and the autonomy rule are d1109-selftasks-run's: from Standard the changes are made by the agent (the planFix context: no read-back, no Inbox echo) and listed with an Undo each, unless a lookup in that turn returned records (d1109-chat-guard's recordsRead: then they are read back at every level); at Advisor and Assisted, or when the set asks first, one composed read-back with Yes and No. Why: the owner's 'autonomy level deciding when it asks first', the same in chat as in a run.

Changes the person names in their own words stay the person's instruction and are read back; several in one line become one question. Why: design §3.9's read-back holds for interpreted instructions; one question per line, never a second card left in the Inbox.
The session page gets an Undo on each change line, from the change log row the event names. Why: 'each change shown with one Undo' where the person sees it.
Changes shows 'In a session' and the agent's name for an agent's change; the task drawer shows what the agent did. Why: design §5 rule 3 (names) and 'every change shown'.
The suggestion card shows its changes open. Why: the person approves what they can read.

fix_tasks takes no request text from the model: its only parameter is the project; the code passes the person's message of that turn verbatim (at most 500 characters) as the request. Why: the design says the person's words are the request; a model-written request could carry text the person never said.

SC-12 (was ST-4): an agent's change says so where it is stored: task.ts's reasons 'Changed by the agent: …', 'Added by the agent: <why>', 'Split from "Style the page" by the agent', 'Dropped by the agent: same as "Add the README"'; never 'by you' for the agent, never an id or 'via chat'. Why: every change shown, plainly, by who made it (design §5 rule 3).

SC-13 (was ST-15): the critic's session review counts a task the agent split, or dropped as a duplicate, as replaced, not as planned and left undone. Why: a correct fix must not lower the plan's grade.

Nothing changed.' (the time from the wait; this area's sentence); under next or a grant it runs on the other credential with its cost in the reply. Why: D5's 'when the app says it waits, nothing moves' covers every call; the chat path is this area's.

triage.item: Changing the web search offer mid-run (max_uses down, or the tool dropped) voids the prompt cache: a quarter to a third of a research run's cost is cache rewrites
triage.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live2-result.json research F3; model-calls-final.jsonl seq 9-10 (read 0, wrote 46,770) and seq 31-34
triage.note: Keep the web_search definition (max_uses and the domain lists) byte-identical for the run while it stays affordable, and keep every limit in code: max_uses is fixed once at the run's start from the smaller of the task's searches left (ten over all its runs) and what the money below the run's wrap-up line pays; every call that offers the tool counts the full max_uses in its pre-call worst case; at the first call where the searches left or the money below the line no longer cover it (or the wrap-up was told), the tool is dropped for the rest of the run and never re-added: one cache rewrite, once, instead of one per call. No limit relies on text: a server tool is billed whatever the text says, and ADR 0107's guarantee that a search never eats the reserve kept to finish (fixup-web-search B1, ADR 0112 amendment) holds. Teach PromptCacheSim the API's web-search/max_uses invalidation. Amend ADR 0107 point 9 and the ADR 0112 note on fewer searches near the line. Avoidable waste per run is about USD 0.07-0.11. Root cause at 931ed52: Holds at 931ed52: packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts:563-583 recomputes maxUses every call from the money below the line; :632-643 leaves webSearch out when 0; packages/runtime/src/provider/anthropic.ts:280-282 appends the tool per call (its comment assumes the tools mark protects the cache); testenv/src/provider/prompt-cache.ts:96-131 ignores req.webSearch, so tests never see the rewrite. Check revision: ["decision corrected (adversarial check spec_problems: 'enforced in the estimate and in text, never by editing the tools' dropped the code limit of ADR 0107/0112; verified at loop.ts:555-583 and ADR 0107 web-search point 4)"]

wave7_live_check_after_merge: After the whole wave is merged, the full suite is green, CI is green on Windows and Linux and the Desktop app workflow ran, the session lead walks six journeys with the real model (details and pass criteria: /tmp/frbench/phaseE7-live.md). Cap USD 4.00 in total, stopping at a clean point; GitHub only on joelwellbournewood/forerunner-sandbox; nothing printed or committed of any key. (1) Merging, about USD 1.10, bench-live: a 3-task chain left at 'You press Merge' (Overview, the dependents' words, Open this version, Merge in order as merge commits, Files within a minute without a session, Take this work out naming the dependent), then a 2-task chain whose first PR is squash-merged on GitHub's website (the dependent rebuilt, only its own commits, merges cleanly), then 'Merge automatically after review' with one task. (2) Credentials, about USD 0.20, on the routed provider (no --provider flag; bench-live ignores the vault): an invalid key in the bench's vault gives one 'Anthropic refused your API key' card and a waiting task; saving the real key starts it by itself; a research plan card says where it runs and why. (3) Budgets, about USD 0.90, bench-live: a coder task whose budget is about three times the reserve its run's log names hears the wrap-up, pauses with a local commit, and Continue finishes it with one review; a tiny budget (CHF 0.02) pauses with the save only and no wrap-up text; Cancel on a paused task names the stuck dependent. (4) Research with web search, about USD 1.00, bench-live: the server tool with max_uses at most 10, blocks sent back unchanged, no 400 (a '*.' block-list entry included), sources only from opened pages, the cost well under 2026-11-02's USD 1.32; then 'Only these websites: developer.mozilla.org' refuses another site and the report names the rule. (5) Costs, about USD 0.40: smoke.cjs --live on a fresh bench, each kind within about x2 of the plan card's estimate, cache reads after the first call. (6) The window: the Desktop app workflow's window check on Windows with Ctrl+click on Inbox (no model cost). Reserve about USD 0.40 for one retry. The subscription-only items (Claude Code stopped at a budget stop and counted once; the page reader, the WebSearch lists and the wrapper on the subscription; the SDK refusal card) go to the owner's checklist step 6, with what to look for; the three owner questions go to the owner with the U-entries. Findings go to a fix round with the same pipeline; spend is added to NEXT-SESSION.md.
wave7_left_out: The status on GitHub as one issue per project (the owner's 'status' decision), the standard repository guide ('repo_guide') and the collaboration module ('collab'): wave 8, after the running collaboration audit (wf_841cec48-831). Wave 7 leaves room: fix/decisions' status_pull_request switch and the status PR stay as they are until wave 8 replaces them (the owner's 'status' decision supersedes that session-lead default; 'merge-in-app' lists the status PR as a docs PR that merges only on the person's click, and 'merged-copy''s lock covers its write); no wave 7 area removes the docs/status.md template ('No docs/status.md in repositories' is wave 8's); the merge record carries agent_id and the paused work is per install, and sharing them across installs or people is the collaboration module's.

Choosing the starting merge mode by reading the repository at linking (automatic checks, Pages or deployments from main): the owner chose 'you press Merge' as every project's default; the automatic mode's change card states the risk in words instead.
'Give this session CHF N more' between tasks (research option D) and raising a running task's budget (option E): not asked for; 'Continue (CHF N more)' starts the next session at once instead.
Anthropic's task budget (beta) and the Agent SDK's alpha taskBudget on the subscription: later, as a measured trial, only if tasks pass as often.
Web search's dynamic filtering (search run from code execution): later; the first version sends the tool without it.

Reading the home or office network, a global 'never these sites' list, robots.txt in Forerunner's reader (the owner was told the two readers differ there), and reading pages through a proxy (only the plain sentence is built).

Running Claude Code inside the Docker sandbox so the subscription can run commands: an untested idea; the chooser and the 'Code tasks that need commands' setting cover the gap for now, with the plan card saying when tests will not run.
Linking the person's own working copy of a repository: the owner said no ('own_folder'); the PC copy stays Forerunner's own under its data folder.

Stacked pull requests, holding a dependent task until its dependency is merged, and one pull request per session: rejected in the research (merge order on the person, the stall the owner met, a large rework).

Anthropic's terms question on storing a Claude.ai token for the Agent SDK: only Anthropic can settle it; the subscription reader is still built because the owner decided 'on both credentials', and web search is built on the API key first.
Live checks that need a Claude subscription token (no token in the cloud environment): the owner's checklist step 6.
The merge of wave 6 (stops, asking, decisions, verification with their fix-ups) and CI green on it: a precondition, not wave 7 work; every wave 7 fixer starts from that merge.

Three owner questions are not left out but built with a stated default and asked in their U-entries (AGENTS.md: a choice about what a person sees goes to the owner as options): what 'wait' means with a second credential ('credential-limits', U-078), whether commands become a hard need on projects with dependencies ('credential-chooser', U-078), and the 'Local only' copy back when the person changed a file during a run ('merged-copy', U-037). The session lead puts their answers into the areas before those areas merge, or the built default stands.

Review points narrowed or corrected, with the reason: (1) 'budget-stop''s pause rule: the review would pause a run whose 'Left to do:' list has items even without a wrap-up; built narrower (a wrap-up in this run and items left, or a budget stop), because a pause card would otherwise name a limit that was not reached. (2) 'credential-limits''s bench step: there is no `--provider none`; the routed provider runs with no --provider flag, and the bench gets `--provider bench-api` (the routed provider pointed at the stand-in, only in a repository checkout). (3) The no-replay marker: both of the review's options are built (the deps base with --no-ff, and the marker kept until the branch is rebuilt). (4) The size review's splits are taken (merge-record and dependent-branches, merged-copy and merged-actions, polish-desktop and polish), and 'credentials' is split too (credential-limits and credential-chooser), because with the review's additions it was the largest area; 'polish' keeps its key so handoffs.json['polish'] still reaches it. (5) The old planned group ['cost', 'polish'] is replaced by wave 7's groups, not kept beside them, so neither area runs twice. Nothing else in the review was rejected: every problem's evidence was read at the scratch merge 6488a14 and holds.
wave7_owner_questions: U-078: what 'When my first choice runs out mid-session: wait' means when a second credential could serve. Built: (a) nothing moves onto the other credential: the stopped task and the session's other tasks on that credential wait for its reset and start by themselves (owner-answers.md section 2's words: 'switching moves work from plan limits onto money'). Option for the owner: (b) only the stopped task waits while the others go on to the other credential, as today (ADR 0100 point 4), with the stopped task's start scheduled at the reset. Changing the answer changes one rule in the pick and the sentences, not the tests' structure.

U-078: should running commands become a hard need for code tasks on a project with dependencies to install? Without commands the project's checks are skipped (project-checks.ts:105-108), so under the default 'my first choice anyway' such a task on the subscription gets neither its own tests nor the project's. Built: the owner's default, with the plan card saying the tests will not run there. Options: (a) keep it; (b) commands become a hard need for such projects, which sends most code work to the API key (money); (c) a third value of the setting, 'the API key when the project has dependencies'.

U-037: when the person changed a file in 'Local only' while a run was using it, what does the copy back do? Built: (a) the person's file wins and the agent's version is kept beside it, with one sentence in the task's result (nothing is lost). Options for the owner: (b) the agent's version wins and the person's is kept beside it; (c) the folder is read-only for the person while a run uses it.
